title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
topics: runtime upgrade to 2.4.1 and kernel compatibility
summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Covered current networking blockers (NAT/egress, route tables), plan for runtime upgrade (2.4.1) to address occasional tokenization regression, review of latency numbers from last test, and concrete next steps: updated ip ranges, SE to run larger-context latency benchmark, security to review SOC2/KMS notes. Agreed target for production-ready checklist and timeline for pilot completion.
next_steps: Redwood to share updated VPC peering guide and explicit IP ranges for 10.7.0.0/16 by 2027-09-10
Ethan to run 16k-context latency/throughput benchmark against pilot cluster and upload logs to shared drive by 2027-09-16
Aurelia Security (Lena) to review KMS/HSM integration doc and confirm compliance gaps by 2027-09-14
Schedule in-person netops window for route table changes (Marcus + Redwood) on 2027-09-15
AE (Sofia) to send pricing/commit options once final perf numbers are in (target 2027-09-17)
action_items: Ethan Li - run 16k-context benchmark with quantized model variant, attach logs - due 2027-09-16
Sofia Martinez - share updated VPC peering guide + ip list - due 2027-09-10
Lena Ortiz - review KMS/HSM integration doc and list compliance questions - due 2027-09-14
Marcus Chen - coordinate firewall rule change and confirm egress/NAT path - due 2027-09-15

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-09 10:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Sofia, Ethan, Priya, Marcus, Lena, Tom

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes. Quick agenda — quick networking update, upgrade notes, perf numbers, then next steps.
[00:12] Priya Desai: Yep sounds good. Marcus is going to start with the network, he's been blocked a bit.
[00:18] Marcus Chen: Hey, yeah so the main blocker is egress, the pilot subnet doesn't have NAT gateway access to the region yet and our security team flagged cross-account peering. We scoped peering but need explicit ip ranges from Redwood.
[00:31] Ethan Li: Right ok — we sent the initial ranges but we'll follow up with CIDR blocks. We found some customers prefer an explicit list to lock down route tables.
[00:40] Marcus Chen: The peering itself is fine, it's more the firewall side — we need ports and ephemeral ranges for the KV cache traffic and control plane.
[00:50] Lena Ortiz: For Security, we also need details on KMS calls, whether any keys are proxied through Redwood or if they stay in our HSM. Also audit log retention is a question.
[01:02] Sofia Martinez: Great point. We'll share the KMS/HSM integration doc. To clarify, for Private mode the control plane talks to your KMS over customer-managed keys, Redwood doesn't hold plaintext keys. But we'll put that in writing.
[01:15] Tom Baker: Quick Q — is there any expected downtime for the runtime upgrade you mentioned? The PM team wants to plan releases.
[01:22] Ethan Li: The upgrade to runtime 2.4.1 is mostly a rolling restart; there shouldn't be major downtime — maybe a minute per node as the runtime swaps kernels. We do recommend a canary window. Also there's a small tokenizer change in 2.4.1 that fixed a correctness regression, we tested on staging.
[01:38] Priya Desai: We saw the tokenization hiccup in last week's test where a few sentences were cut; that was worrying. Is 2.4.1 guaranteed to fix that?
[01:46] Ethan Li: It addresses the specific regression we saw — not 100% guarantee in all edge cases but it's been validated on the same model family you run. We'll include model variant checks in the release notes.
[01:57] Marcus Chen: If we upgrade, we need kernel compatibility with our older GPUs; can you confirm quantization paths aren't impacted?
[02:05] Ethan Li: Quantization-friendly paths remain, but there are kernel selector changes that will pick slightly different kernels for small-batch workloads. We have a fallback path to preserve throughput. We'll share a compatibility matrix.
[02:20] Sofia Martinez: Jumping to perf numbers — Ethan, can you walk through the latency and throughput from last run?
[02:25] Ethan Li: Sure. Last run: 2.2.0 runtime, model redwood-vicuna-13b-quant, 8k context, average p95 latency 420ms for single-stream requests, batch of 8 throughput 120 tokens/s, cost estimate came out about 0.018 USD per 1k tokens in current config. After switching to the alternative kernel in staging we saw p95 drop to 370ms. There's some noise though, Marcus's environment had an extra proxy hop which added ~30ms.
[02:52] Marcus Chen: Yea that proxy is legacy — we can test without it in the next run.
[02:56] Lena Ortiz: On the cost side, can we get more explicit guidance on batching/caching tradeoffs? Our legal wants to understand data residency and cache TTLs.
[03:06] Ethan Li: Yes — Redwood Private supports prefix/KV caching with customer-controlled TTLs. For PII-sensitive flows you can set TTL to zero and rely on per-request KV. We'll send the batching/caching guide.
[03:17] Priya Desai: For benchmarks, can you run a run with 16k context? We expect a few larger documents.
[03:23] Ethan Li: Absolutely — I can run 16k with the quantized 13b variant and also test the 70B smaller-slicing config if you like. That will show memory and KV behavior.
[03:31] Tom Baker: That would be great, please include logs and latency distribution, not just averages.
[03:36] Ethan Li: Yep will push full artifacts to the shared drive.
[03:40] Sofia Martinez: Ok circling back to security — Lena, anything else?
[03:44] Lena Ortiz: Just make the KMS/HSM doc explicit about what API calls look like and an example of audit logs, also SAML/SSO provisioning steps for RBAC. We want an end-to-end audit trail.
[03:54] Sofia Martinez: We'll include SSO/SAML setup steps and an RBAC mapping example. For audits, Redwood writes a dedicated audit log feed you can ship to your SIEM.
[04:04] Priya Desai: Perfect.
[04:06] Sofia Martinez: Quick note on routing: Marcus if you can open the route table change window for 9/15, we can coordinate to flip the peering and test an egress path without the legacy proxy.
[04:15] Marcus Chen: I'll schedule it and ping the list.
[04:18] Ethan Li: One more technical note — we noticed the model variant used a slightly different KV cache eviction policy which can cause cold-start blips; for production we'll recommend warm caches and pre-warm scripts. We'll share pre-warm script example.
[04:33] Tom Baker: Pre-warm script would help our QA run a canary. Please include parameterized examples.
[04:38] Ethan Li: Will do.
[04:40] Sofia Martinez: Any blockers on pricing? We wanted to get provisional pricing once perf numbers are finalized.
[04:44] Priya Desai: No blockers, just need numbers to compare to our internal infra TCO.
[04:48] Sofia Martinez: Ok we'll produce pricing ranges after the benchmark run.
[04:51] Priya Desai: Timeline wise, what's realistic to be production-ready?
[04:55] Sofia Martinez: If we clear the network egress and the 16k perf looks good, I'd say target end of month for pilot completion — contingent on compliance sign-off. So around 2027-09-30.
[05:05] Marcus Chen: That works.
[05:07] Lena Ortiz: We'll aim to close compliance questions earlier, 9/14 is our cutover for KMS review.
[05:12] Sofia Martinez: Great. Recap of next steps...
[05:16] Sofia Martinez: Ethan to run benchmark and upload logs; I will share the IP ranges and VPC peering doc; Lena will review KMS; Marcus will schedule route changes; Tom will share the success criteria. We'll reconvene same time next week.
[05:29] Priya Desai: Thanks all.
[05:31] Sofia Martinez: Thanks, end of call.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cache" appears as "K V cache" at times), some speaker labels auto-attributed. References: Redwood VPC peering guide (link shared in chat), KMS/HSM integration doc (to be shared).
